review_notes:
I read the whole file and compared it with ChainSplit.lean (integral_chain_filter_le, integrable_finite_test_count) and with other uses of graphPerpND in the repo.

The only exact repeat is the measurability proof for {w | ‖graphPerpND w (…)‖ ≤ W}. It appears as hF at lines 46–52 and inside the integrability proof at lines 281–286. Both use `apply measurableSet_le _ measurable_const; unfold graphPerpND; fun_prop`. That is about three lines of routine unfolding plus fun_prop. The rubric excludes this kind of short, routine step, so I did not report it. ClassConditional.lean has a related measurability argument, but it is structured differently (a sum of ite terms with case splits).

The other blocks that look alike are mostly one-off exponent arithmetic with Real.rpow, such as the `R^(…)` rewrites with `congr 1; ring`. They use different exponents and different hypotheses, and each is a short calculation. I found no nontrivial reasoning that two proofs share and that a single lemma could replace. I did not try to compile anything, so this is a judgement from reading the source.
